correctness.rationale: For every k≥1 and all integer d_j≥1, affine normalization to standard simplices is legitimate. At vertex 0 the strict inward simplex tangent cone has all coordinate components >0; at vertex e_i it has u_j>0 for all j≠i and Σ_j u_j<0. Any two such cones are disjoint (for d=1 the two open rays are disjoint). Product vertex tangent cones are Cartesian products, so two different product vertices have disjoint illuminating-direction sets. Thus any illuminating direction can serve at most one product vertex; summing unit requirements across these pairwise disjoint direction sets proves i*(P)≥f0(P) as well as i(P)≥f0(P). One strictly inward vector at each vertex illuminates all boundary points because a face point has a subset of the active facets at a vertex of the same face; hence i(P)≤f0(P) and also i*(P)≤f0(P). The inequalities d+1≤2^d (equality only d=1) and d+1≤3·2^{d−2} for d≥2 (equality only d=2), with other factors at most 2^{d_j}, give the sharp n-dimensional noncube bound and exact equality family. Independent checker reconstructed facet sign tests for integer directions d=1..6 and enumerated integer partitions n≤12, with no contradictions; those finite checks are corroborative, not infinite proof. Definition of finite-support fractional measures, nonzero directions and boundary points, n≥1 edge case all checked. Correctness does not rescue covered originality.

Any two different vertices v,w of a product of simplices disagree at some factor j. A barycentric coordinate λ of that simplex has λ(v_j)=1, λ(w_j)=0. The hyperplanes λ=1 and λ=0, extended trivially across other factors, are parallel supports of P, so the entire V(P) is antipodal.

originality.rationale: A decisive published general theorem already implies both purported contributions. Naszódi (2009), Fractional illumination of convex bodies, equation (1.1), proves a(K)≤i*(K)≤i(K), where a(K) is maximum antipodal-set cardinality. Every pair of distinct vertices in a Cartesian product of simplices is antipodal using a single differing factor’s barycentric coordinate hyperplanes λ=0 and λ=1; thus a(P)≥f0(P). For every polytope, one vertex-inward direction per vertex illuminates every boundary point, giving i(P)≤f0(P). Hence i(P)=i*(P)=f0(P) is an immediate prior corollary. The sharp cube uniqueness and 3·2^{n−2} gap are then elementary maximization of ∏(d_j+1) under Σd_j=n. Relevant exact, alias, antipodality, table and semantic searches and three primary full-text/section readings support this statement. The submitted Resultary entry itself is not counted as independent prior.
residual_risks: A prior source may also print the exact product formula under another name, but historical exact-wording discovery is unnecessary because Naszódi’s stronger 2009 published result logically implies it.
The separate rank-k antipodality preprint concerns a broader variant; neither that manuscript nor the cube-local theorem is used to claim the exact formula on its own.

source_inspections.evidence: For any convex body K, Eq. (1.1) gives a(K)≤i*(K)≤i(K). Thus ALL product vertices form an antipodal set, providing the exact f0(P) lower bound already via Eq. (1.1). The standard one-inward-direction-per-vertex polytope upper bound is i(P)≤f0(P).

value.rationale: Illumination of simplex products is a natural dimension-uniform Banach/convex-geometry question, but the submitted equality is already a one-paragraph corollary of Naszódi’s general antipodal lower bound using a single simplex barycentric coordinate and the standard vertex upper bound. The only further statement, a 3/4 noncube gap with equality for one triangular factor, is the elementary inequality d+1≤2^d and its first strict case d=2. Consequently there is no previously undetermined exact invariant, nontrivial structural boundary, new general theorem, or meaningful unknown classification beyond prior implications. Correctness and all-dimensional scope alone do not make the covered algebraic specialization independently valuable.
residual_risks: The product-of-simplices family remains mathematically canonical; a genuinely different new structural invariant could be valuable, but none is asserted in the final audited claim.
